title: Jupyter MCP management routes allow backend hijacking and a later Host-header bypass
summary: Datalayer documents missing authentication and browser-origin checks on standalone HTTP management routes. Attackers can replace the active notebook backend or stop it. A later Host-header check can also be bypassed in insecure no-auth mode.

severity.rationale: A malicious page or network caller can redirect the assistant to attacker-controlled infrastructure. The documented impact is notebook-session integrity and data exposure, rather than unconditional host code execution.

affected.note: The original authentication and DNS-rebinding advisories list versions through 1.0.2 and no patched version.
The later bypass advisory lists versions below 2.1.3.

exposure: Original flaws affect standalone streamable-http management routes even with MCP_TOKEN set. The later full backend-hijack bypass requires insecure no-auth mode; token mode still protects state-changing routes.

params.instructions: Check jupyter-mcp-server version, standalone HTTP transport and authentication mode. Review the three vendor advisories; a token on /mcp alone does not establish management-route protection.

remediation.details: Require bearer authentication on management routes and enforce browser-origin checks. Upgrade past the later bypass to 2.1.3 or later and verify these controls before exposure. The original advisories do not identify a patched release.
remediation.risk: Medium. Authentication and listener changes can interrupt clients.

verification: Verify unauthenticated management requests and untrusted browser origins are rejected without changing the active backend.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
Added the vendor severity for each advisory, including the two published CVSS scores and vectors, after independent review identified the omissions.
